items.title: Mozambique’s exchange rate reform aims for gradual shift towards a market-led exchange rate – minister
items.summary: “We also have the chapter on exchange rate reform, which aims to move gradually and in a guided manner towards a market-led exchange rate,” Carla Loveira said, presenting measures under way or planned at a meeting with businesspeople in Maputo The position, expressed during a meeting held as part of a Business Breakfast dedicated to fiscal policy, the business environment and private-sector priorities for the country’s economic growth, organised by the Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA), comes amid debate over difficulties in accessing foreign currency and the process by which the central bank sets the exchange rate In practice, due to the lack of access to foreign currency through the banking system, businesspeople end up resorting to buying currency through alternative channels, at rates considerably above the official exchange rate.

items.title: INE records over 14,000 registered non-profit entities in Mozambique
items.summary: Maputo, 30 Oct (AIM) – Mozambique’s National Statistics Institute (INE) has recorded 14,462 formally registered non-profit entities, as part of the 3rd Business Census (CEMPRE 2025-2026). According to the census – which was conducted between September 2025 and May 2026, aiming to collect and update information on the structure of the Mozambican business sector, non-profit institutions – the country has 112,784 formally registered companies. The study points out that these non-profit institutions employ 136,269 people and generate approximately 117.4 billion meticais in annual revenue (1.8 billion US dollars at the current exchange rate). 50.7 percent of these institutions are associations, followed by religious organizations at 45.5 percent. The southern provinces Inhambane and of Gaza, and the central province of Manica, account together 67.4 percent of the country’s non-profit institutions. On the other hand, INE recorded the formal existence of 112.784 companies in the country, which corresponds to 80.1 percent.

items.title: Tennessee woman Christa Pike describes pain after failed execution
items.summary: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain a month after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee. Her lawyers want her death sentence reduced to life, while the state governor has ordered an investigation Death row inmate Christa Pike said Friday that she remained in constant pain and struggled to speak a month after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee Her lawyers have urged Governor Bill Lee to reduce her death sentence to life imprisonment, but he has indicated that it will remain unchanged unless the courts intervene In her first public statement since the failed execution, Pike said she had expected to die but instead woke up alone and confused in a hospital bed "There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain," she said. "My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts.

items.title: Ceasefire allows evacuation from devastated Russian-occupied Oleshky
items.summary: Watch: How will the evacuation of Oleshky unfold? Hundreds of residents of the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have been evacuated, Russian and Ukrainian authorities have said, following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump "Everything unfolded without any incidents, and both sides noted the high level of organisation," Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said Ukrainian authorities confirmed the evacuees were on their way to southern Russia, from where they will travel on to Ukraine through Belarus Melania Trump said that "all elements of the convoy, including the safe passageway in and out of Oleshky, was established through mutual agreement between Russian and Ukrainian leaders" A ceasefire - the longest and most widespread since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 - has been in force in the entire frontline region of Kherson since Tuesday, allowing for the road out of Oleshky to be demined Residents who wished to leave had a four-hour window to do so on Friday.

items.title: Ethiopia acquires Russian fighter jets and air defence systems amid war in Tigray
items.summary: The acquisition of fighter jets comes amid ongoing tensions with Eritrea Ethiopia has received 12 Su-35 fighter jets from Russia, as fighting intensified in the northern Tigray region neighbouring Eritrea Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who is attending the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, described the acquisition as a "milestone" that would boost Ethiopia's defence capacity He said Ethiopia and Russia had agreed on the deal several years ago and the warplanes had come ahead of schedule. He also said that Ethiopia had plans to acquire four S-400 air defence systems from Moscow The Ethiopian leader said the military hardware was essential to protect the country from external threats Inside the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow Abiy, who described Russian President Vladimir Putin, "as a close friend of Ethiopia", said Ethiopia had now become the first country in sub‑Saharan Africa to own this kind of "advanced combat technology" "If we fail to build this capability, surviving as a country in our region will become difficult.

items.title: Careless dismissals give Australia route to series win
items.summary: The winner of the third Test will finish the series top of the International Cricket Council's Test rankings Third Test, Cape Town (day three of five) South Africa 329 & 140-4: Ackerman 62; Starc 2-29 Australia 429: Inglis 102; Harmer 4-104 Batters carelessly gifting wickets to Australia... we have been here before This time it was not England helping their opponents, although they will have taken note with a tour of South Africa to come this winter South Africa's attempt to fight back in the decisive third Test against Australia was hurt by two poor strokes on day three Having taken the last six Australian wickets for 99 runs in the morning despite Josh Inglis' second Test century, the Proteas began their second innings facing a deficit of exactly 100 They needed runs from their experienced opener and number three. Neither Aiden Markram nor David Bedingham could deliver By the end, even captain Temba Bavuma had been tempted into a wild swipe to fall for 35.
